headline: Indigenous Fire Guardians Cut Peru Wildfires by 81%
meta_description: Indigenous Asháninka communities in Peru have slashed wildfires by 81% using traditional knowledge combined with modern satellite technology and drone monitori…
summary_short: Indigenous communities in Peru are preventing wildfires through a groundbreaking programme combining ancestral knowledge with real-time satellite imagery and drones.
body:
Wildfires across 45 Indigenous Asháninka communities in Peru have plummeted from 25 fires in 2023 to just nine in 2024, protecting 2,648 hectares of forest from burning down to 492 hectares—an 81% reduction. The success comes through Paamari, a collaboration between the Central Asháninka of the Ene River (CARE) and Cool Earth, a charity supporting Indigenous climate action. Community members like Romer Quentimari Garcia, a certified brigadista in Osherato, now work with real-time satellite imagery, drones and radio systems to detect and extinguish fires before they spread. In 2025, the territory saw zero wildfires as communities successfully stopped emerging threats.

This achievement stands in stark contrast to Peru's wider crisis. Just two years earlier, a historic drought triggered the country's worst wildfire season on record, with over 10,000 fires destroying 63,000 hectares—an area larger than Chicago. The Paamari programme's success lies in blending centuries-old Indigenous knowledge with modern technology, according to David Torres, a coordinator with CARE. Where difficult terrain prevents national fire crews from responding quickly, Indigenous communities become the first and last line of defence.

The model also challenges restrictive government policies that prohibit all burning, even traditional prescribed burns used for crop management. Instead, Paamari demonstrates that meaningful collaboration works. As Julio Acosta, Cool Earth's forest data manager, explains, when local people own the project from the start, conservation outcomes become lasting. Academic research backs this: a 2026 University of British Columbia analysis of 111 peer-reviewed papers found that Indigenous-managed lands delivered conservation outcomes comparable to or exceeding protected areas. As Quentimari Garcia reflects, "The forest is life"—and now, that life is being protected by those who know it best.
quick_facts: Wildfires dropped 81% across 45 Asháninka communities, 2023 to 2024
Romer Quentimari Garcia uses drones and satellite imagery to detect fires
Paamari programme launched in 2023 by CARE and Cool Earth charity
Zero wildfires recorded in territory throughout 2025
